answer: Yes. Low relative elevation (TPI, 102 m window, 2 m DEM, lower = more likely) separates Ida's 159 high-water marks from 3,180 random controls within 500 m. Point AUC is 0.71 and site-level AUC 0.78 (83 sites; bootstrap 95% CI 0.71-0.85). Sink depth does slightly better: point AUC 0.73, site AUC 0.81 (CI 0.75-0.86). The CIs overlap, so neither clearly wins. Both are moderate discriminators, not predictors. 79% of marks sit below their local mean versus 51% of controls. The measures partly agree. Spearman between sink depth and TPI is -0.41 on all points and -0.58 at marks. Of marks in a sink (>=0.15 m), 54% are also TPI-low (<=-0.5 m). Results depend on window size: site AUC is 0.72 at 50 m, 0.78 at 102 m and 0.79 at 202 m. They are largely, not wholly, redundant. Controls are unverified non-flood points.
traps_or_caveats: Controls are random points within 500 m of marks, not verified dry places (Ida flooded widely). Some controls may have flooded, which would understate AUC; marks are presence-only so false alarms cannot be measured.

Controls sit near marks, so the AUC measures local contrast within 500 m and cannot be extrapolated to citywide screening. Marks are also not independent, so site-level AUC (median per site vs its controls) is the more honest figure.
AUC is moderate (0.71-0.81); an AUC of 0.5 would be no skill. The sink vs TPI difference is within bootstrap CIs. TPI depends on window size, so the result is not a single number.

Header on line 2 (line 1 is a citation) and feet-to-meters conversion were handled by reusing read_marks. Interior marks (31, regex-flagged on description text, imperfect) are reported separately; street-only results are similar for both measures (site AUC ~0.80).

DEM is bare earth: storm sewers, buildings, curbs are ignored, and sewer backups and basement flooding are not terrain-driven. Interior marks scoring well on sinks (AUC 0.90, 19 sites, wide CI) should not be over-interpreted.

Tiles are processed one at a time with Fill and focal means, so values near tile edges are biased. Excluding points within 60 m of a tile edge changed nothing material (site AUC 0.81 sink, 0.78 TPI). Controls with DEM below 0.5 m (open water or missing) were skipped, as in the original script.
Observed depth (height above ground) is weakly related to both measures at street marks (Spearman 0.33 sink, -0.35 TPI, n=121), so these separate flooded places but do not estimate depth.

TPI uses a 51x51 cell rectangular mean. My own NaN-aware scipy mean reproduced ArcPy FocalStatistics identically for 51 cells (checked via AUC identity). I ran the score outside score_layer.run, using my own AUC/bootstrap code (proveit.score auc/spearman).
